Subject: SIG intake - SDLC evidence request for vendor assessment

Hi Connor / Redwood team,

Thanks for agreeing to the SIG intake call earlier. As a follow-up the assessor team asked for a compact package of artifacts to validate your Secure SDLC controls:

- Code review policy and a sample review record (last 90 days)
- CI/CD pipeline config showing gated deploys and ephemeral credentials
- Secrets provisioning and rotation evidence (KMS/HSM integration notes)
- Change management log for production releases (last 6 months)

Can you provide a short manifest of files you will supply and a single shared location (Drive link or secure SFTP) where we can pull the artifacts? We need this by EOD Thursday to keep our audit timeline.

If any items are sensitive (redactions required), note the redaction in the manifest.

Regards,
Luis

TriadBank

Team — forwarding TriadBank's artifact ask. We need a concise package (single folder) and a short manifest mapping each artifact to the control it satisfies. Priorities below:

1) Code review sampling + policy (include PR IDs, reviewers, and sign-off traces). Redact developer emails if necessary.
2) CI pipeline snapshot & examples of gated deploys (pipeline yaml, step logs showing approval gates).
3) Secrets management notes (KMS key rotation schedule, HSM usage if any, and who has admin access).
4) Change log for prod releases covering the last six months (tickets, approvers, dates).

Irene — can you lead collection for (1) and (4)? Start with samples that are representative (not exhaustive).
Karthik — can you export the pipeline config and an example run that shows gated deployment and ephemeral credential issuance?
Marissa — please prepare a 1-page manifest (PDF) mapping artifacts to SIG questions and mark anything that needs redaction.

Aim for a single shared Drive folder and send Luis a link when ready. If we need an NDA addendum for any raw logs, flag it immediately.

Thanks,
Connor

Connor / team,

Quick update on artifacts. I pulled representative items and attached a preliminary manifest. Attachments:
- sdlc_evidence_manifest.pdf (manifest mapping artifacts to SIG control IDs)
- code_review_sampling.zip (redacted PR excerpts; filenames inside: PR-4213.txt, PR-4456.txt)
- ci_pipeline_snapshot.csv (exported pipeline steps including gated approvals)

Notes / clarifications:
- Code review: we use GitHub branch protection and require at least 1 reviewer plus automated checks. The zip includes two PRs from the last 60 days; developer emails are redacted and replaced with role tags (e.g., reviewer: eng-lead).
- CI/CD: our pipeline implements a manual approval gate before the deploy job that is scoped to members of the Release Managers group. The CSV indicates the job names and timestamps. Ephemeral credentials are issued by our ephemeral-agent service integrated with KMS (see short comment in the manifest).
- Secrets rotation: rotation schedule is documented in the manifest and references the rotation automation job. KMS key metadata is in the manifest (key id redacted). Production-grade keys are managed via the cloud KMS provider; HSM not used at present.
- Change management: I included a list of production releases for the last 6 months with ticket IDs and approvers (columns in the CSV).

Marissa — final manifest review and PDF polish as discussed. Karthik — if you can export a sanitized pipeline run log (including the approval gate event), that will help the assessor validate the gating behavior.

Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

[attachment stubs: sdlc_evidence_manifest.pdf (PDF), code_review_sampling.zip (ZIP), ci_pipeline_snapshot.csv (CSV)]

Hi Luis — attaching the evidence manifest and a curated set of artifacts in one Drive folder for your review: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bTriadBankEvidence

Summary of what we've shared in the folder (high level):
- SDLC Manifest (sdlc_evidence_manifest.pdf): maps artifacts to SIG/CAIQ items and notes redactions.
- Code review sampling (code_review_sampling.zip): two redacted PR transcriptions that show reviewer sign-offs and automated checks.
- CI pipeline snapshot (ci_pipeline_snapshot.csv): pipeline steps, the manual approval gate entry, and a pointer to the ephemeral credential issuance step.
- Change history (ci_pipeline_snapshot.csv, change-log section): CSV includes release IDs, JIRA links, and approvers.

Two operational notes:
1) KMS key IDs are redacted in the manifest; if you need full key metadata for key attestation we can coordinate a timestamped disclosure under an NDA.
2) Our ephemeral-agent issues short-lived tokens scoped to the deploy job; secret material is never stored in plain text in the pipeline workspace. We included comments in the manifest showing the automation job names.

If you want a quick walkthrough, Irene and Karthik can join a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the artifacts and answer any control-specific questions. Please let us know your availability.

Best,
